t: Closest Node to Path in Tree — Distance Filtering via Double BFS
o: For each query (start, end, node), the path from start to end consists exactly of the vertices v with dist(start, v) + dist(v, end) == dist(start, end). So run three BFS traversals per query — from start, from end, and from node — collect path vertices, and pick the one minimizing dist(node, v). With n, queries <= 1000 this is O(q * n), well within limits. Ties are broken by choosing any closest node (examples show unique answers).
k: Membership on the start-end path is characterized by the metric equality dist(s,v)+dist(v,e)=dist(s,e).
Three BFS runs per query suffice; no LCA machinery is needed at these constraint sizes.

a.i: BFS gives all distances from a source in O(n). Compute distFromStart, distFromEnd, distFromNode; filter vertices satisfying the path equality; return the filtered vertex minimizing distFromNode.
s: Per query: BFS from start, end, and node.
Collect v with ds[v] + de[v] == ds[end]; return argmin dn[v] over those.
a.t: O(q * n) — three linear BFS traversals plus a linear scan per query.
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency and distance arrays.

a.n: Approach 2: LCA-Based Walk Along the Path
a.i: Find the meeting point m = LCA(start, end). The closest node on the path is either the ancestor of `node` lying on the start-m half or on the m-end half. Using binary lifting, locate the deepest ancestor of node that lies on each half (via checking whether an ancestor a of node satisfies dist(a,start)+dist(a,m)==dist(start,m)), and pick whichever of the two candidates is closer to node. This achieves O((n + q) log n).
s: Preprocess binary lifting tables for LCA queries.
Walk from node upward to find the deepest ancestor on segment start..m and on segment m..end; return the closer one.
a.t: O((n + q) log n) with full binary lifting implementation.
a.sp: O(n log n) for lifting tables.

w: The BFS-filtering approach is the one to write: it is short, obviously correct, and fast enough. Pitfall: the path equality must use the tree distance (unique paths), which BFS provides. Follow-up: handle millions of queries — then binary lifting LCA becomes mandatory.
